name: Topical Authority
definition: Evaluates whether an entity has deep, consistent expertise in its claimed subject area. Diluted authority from covering too many topics weakens ranking potential. Google's classifiers weigh topic consistency across domain name, content, reviews, and brand signals. When an entity's identity is split across verticals, each vertical receives less authority than a specialist competitor.

name: Knowledge Graph Entity Mapping
definition: Maps entities to the broader web of trusted organizations, certifications, and industry associations. Schema.org markup, sameAs links, and consistent cross-references between an entity and known organizations allow Google to confidently place the entity within its Knowledge Graph, increasing trust and visibility.

name: Brand Signal Strength
definition: Measures branded search volume and recognition. Entities with strong, growing brand demand receive algorithmic preference and benefit-of-the-doubt in ranking. Weak branded search volume means the site must compete purely on page-level signals without the trust boost that established brands receive.

name: Entity Association Strength
definition: Measures how strongly an entity is connected to other recognized entities in its industry. Without explicit mentions and structured data linking to certifying bodies or manufacturer partner pages, Google's Knowledge Graph cannot confidently connect an entity to the broader web of trusted organizations.

name: Entity Coherence
definition: Measures whether the content presents a consistent business identity with verifiable name, address, certifications, associations, and service history. Generic business descriptions that could be any company score low.

name: Keyword Cannibalization
definition: Detects multiple pages on the same site competing for the same search intent, diluting ranking power and confusing Google about which page to rank.

name: Broken Entity Trust
definition: Identifies inconsistencies between business claims on the page and external signals such as directory listings, reviews, GBP data, or licensing records.

name: Knowledge Graph Alignment
definition: Measures how strongly the entity appears in Google's structured knowledge sources and whether page content aligns with Knowledge Graph data, checked via search signals.

name: Entity Reinforcement
definition: Measures how consistently the entity's identity (name, services, expertise) is reinforced across all pages. Strong reinforcement helps search engines build a confident entity model.

name: Brand Voice Dilution
definition: Detects when content across a site lacks consistent brand voice, often due to multiple content creators, outsourced writing, or AI-generated content mixed with human-written pages.

name: Service Dilution Drift
definition: Detects when secondary services overshadow high-value offerings, causing the entity to be viewed as a 'generalist' rather than a 'specialist' for premium services by topical authority classifiers.

name: Entity Association Weakness
definition: Identifies missing schema links to certifying bodies, industry associations, or known entities. Without these, Google cannot verify professional pedigree beyond self-claims.

name: Cross-Service Cannibalization
definition: Identifies duplicate or highly similar copy across related service pages, causing internal competition that dilutes individual page ranking power through the scaled content classifier.

name: Brand vs Commodity Ratio
definition: Measures branded search volume against generic service searches. A low brand ratio means commodity status, making the entity vulnerable to algorithm updates that favor established brands.

name: Specialization Drift
definition: Detects lumping distinct service categories together in site structure and internal linking, causing failure to capture premium market segments due to generalist perception by niche entity classifiers.

name: Entity Recognition Strength
definition: Evaluates whether Google recognizes the linking source as a defined entity with Knowledge Graph presence, rather than an anonymous domain.

name: Primary Niche Match
definition: Evaluates whether the source and target domains operate in the same or adjacent industry niches. Links from topically relevant sources transfer more authority.

name: Semantic Keyword Overlap
definition: Measures what keywords both the source and target sites share, indicating topical alignment and relevance of the link relationship.

name: Entity Co-occurrence
definition: Checks whether both the source and target entities appear together in search results, indicating Google already associates the two entities.

name: Audience Overlap Probability
definition: Estimates whether the source site's audience would be interested in the target site's content. High overlap indicates a natural, valuable link relationship.

name: Knowledge Graph Proximity
definition: Evaluates whether the source and target entities are connected or closely related in Google's Knowledge Graph, indicating a natural entity relationship.

name: Entity Node Reinforcement
definition: Measures whether this link validates the target's entity identity by connecting it to a recognized source in the same or related domain.

name: Category Drift
definition: Detects content spanning unrelated verticals, service offerings outside core expertise, and sudden pivots to trending topics. Expanding beyond the core category weakens topical authority and fragments accumulated trust signals.

name: Local Prominence & Proximity
definition: Evaluates an entity's authority within specific geographic areas. Prominence decays with distance from the entity's verified location. Without localized content, geotagged project evidence, and location-specific reviews, an entity's geographic authority drops sharply outside its primary market.

name: Geographic Authority
definition: Measures an entity's proven service presence in claimed geographic areas. Service area claims without location-specific proof result in geographic ghosting. Entities claiming broad service areas need localized landing pages, project galleries with geotagged content, and city-specific reviews.

name: Neighborhood Granularity
definition: Measures the specificity of local references such as neighborhoods, streets, landmarks, or districts on the page. References to specific micro-areas rather than just city names strengthen local entity grounding.

name: Local Benchmark Data
definition: Detects the presence of local statistics, pricing benchmarks, regional context, or market-specific data on the page that demonstrates genuine local knowledge.

name: Hyper-Local Landmarks
definition: Detects references to recognizable local places such as parks, intersections, venues, or natural features on the page that anchor the entity to its geography.

name: Service Radius Mapping
definition: Measures whether the site defines a realistic and coherent geographic service area with clear boundaries, rather than claiming an unrealistically large coverage zone.

name: Community Involvement
definition: Detects mentions of local sponsorships, events, charities, or partnerships that demonstrate the entity is an active participant in its local community.

name: Physical Presence Signals
definition: Evaluates whether the business address, phone, map, and operational footprint are verifiable on the page and consistent across directory listings found via search.

name: Staff Bio Localization
definition: Measures whether team members are tied to the local region through bios, profiles, or references that demonstrate they live and work in the area.

name: Regional Competitor Context
definition: Detects whether the content acknowledges or compares with specific local competitors, demonstrating awareness of the actual competitive landscape.

name: Phone Area Code Verification
definition: Checks whether the phone number on the page corresponds with the geographic region being targeted. A mismatched area code undermines local trust signals.

name: Neighborhood Review Clustering
definition: Analyzes whether reviews reference specific neighborhoods, communities, or local details that confirm the entity actually operates in its claimed area.

name: Site Reputation Proximity
definition: Evaluates whether the domain is associated with known spam or low-quality domains via search signals. Proximity to bad neighborhoods in the link graph damages trust.

name: City Modifier Legitimacy
definition: Evaluates whether city-specific pages contain legitimate, unique local content or are just template pages with the city name swapped in. Illegitimate city modifiers trigger doorway page detection.

name: Local Embedding
definition: Measures how strongly the business is positioned within the local community through citations, directory listings, local media mentions, and community participation signals.

name: Geographic Ghosting
definition: Identifies attempts to rank outside the core service radius without local entity proof. The core location anchor fails to stretch, and visibility drops at the county or city line.

name: Primary Category Accuracy
definition: Evaluates whether the declared GBP primary category accurately matches the entity's main service. Miscategorization or multi-trade complexity can create profile dilution risk across primary query signals.

name: Semantic Bio Match
definition: Evaluates whether the business description in the GBP profile semantically matches the actual services offered and the entity's website content.

name: Attribute Accuracy
definition: Checks whether GBP attributes (hours, payment methods, accessibility, amenities) are accurately set and up to date. Incorrect attributes create trust inconsistencies.

name: Centroid Proximity
definition: Evaluates how close the entity's verified address is to the geographic center of the target market. Distance from the search query centroid directly impacts local pack rankings.

name: Service Area Overlap
definition: Measures how much the entity's declared service area overlaps with competitor service areas and whether the coverage claims are realistic.

name: Neighborhood Hyperlocalism
definition: Evaluates whether the GBP listing and reviews contain neighborhood-level references that anchor the entity to specific micro-areas within its market.

name: Hyperlocal Backlinks
definition: Measures links from local organizations, chambers of commerce, local news, community sites, and neighborhood resources that anchor the entity to its geographic area.

name: Entity Proximity Decay
definition: Detects attempts to rank far outside the core service radius without supporting local entity proof. Weak spatial grounding reduces eligibility for premium SERP features.

name: Regulatory Compliance
definition: Verifies that an entity holds required licenses, permits, and regulatory approvals for its claimed services. Cross-references claimed services against required regulatory credentials. Entities advertising regulated services without displaying verifiable license numbers face trust deficits.

name: Technical Certifications
definition: Evaluates industry-standard certifications and manufacturer authorizations. IICRC, NADCA, NATE, and similar credentials validate specialized competency. Verifiable third-party certifications provide independent proof of technical competency. The gap between claimed and proven expertise is a primary trust vulnerability.

name: Missing Privacy & Terms
definition: Checks for required legal and policy pages such as privacy policy or terms of service linked from the page. Missing legal pages signal a less trustworthy operation.

name: Credential Verifiability
definition: Evaluates whether certifications and licenses can be confirmed through external sources. Credentials that link to verification databases score higher than unverifiable badge images.

name: Reputation Alignment
definition: Measures consistency between website claims and what external reviews, directories, and third-party sources say about the entity. Misalignment erodes trust.

name: Policy Transparency
definition: Checks whether privacy policies, terms of service, and other business policies are clearly stated and accessible. Transparent policies signal a legitimate, trustworthy operation.

name: License Crosslinking
definition: Verifies that displayed credentials link to external verification sources such as state licensing board lookups or certification body databases, rather than just showing badge images.

name: Grounded Claims
definition: Specific business claims that ARE verified by external sources such as licensing databases, directory listings, review content, or search-discoverable evidence.

name: Regulatory Licensing Status
definition: Evaluates state and local licensing status by cross-referencing claims against actual regulatory body databases. Specific licenses required for the trade in the specific jurisdiction are identified and verified.

name: Bonding & Insurance
definition: Verifies surety bond status, liability coverage, and workers compensation insurance. Evaluates minimum coverage requirements for the trade and jurisdiction.

name: Trade Association Membership
definition: Evaluates professional association affiliations at national, state, and local levels. BBB accreditation and industry-specific membership programs strengthen entity authority.

name: Operational Competency
definition: Measures permit history, fleet presence, staffing ratios, and response infrastructure as indicators of real operational capability beyond marketing claims.

name: Safety & Compliance
definition: Evaluates safety records, OSHA compliance, environmental permits, and violation history from public records. Critical for trades with regulatory safety requirements.

name: Third-Party Validation
definition: Measures award history, third-party audit results, and platform recognitions from Angi, HomeAdvisor, Nextdoor, or Yelp. Reviews that specifically mention credentials strengthen this signal.

name: Digital Credential Visibility
definition: Evaluates whether credentials are prominently displayed on the website with proper schema markup (hasCredential, certification structured data) and listed in the Google Business Profile.

name: Verification Tier
definition: Evaluates the level of Google verification the business has achieved. Higher verification tiers (video, mail, phone) provide stronger trust signals.

name: Helpful Content System
definition: Sitewide classifier that evaluates whether content is created primarily for users or for search engine rankings. Sales-focused content without genuine expertise triggers suppression. Measures the ratio of sales collateral to genuine expertise content. Sites built to convert traffic rather than educate or demonstrate unique experience receive a sitewide dampening signal that amplifies other suppressors.

name: E-E-A-T Experience Signals
definition: Evaluates first-hand, demonstrable expertise through authentic content. Project photos, case studies, named experts, and real-world proof establish experience authority. Content is classified as having genuine experience when it includes unique visuals, named personnel, specific project details, and information that could only come from hands-on work. Generic or stock content fails this evaluation.

name: Information Gain
definition: Measures whether a page adds new, useful information beyond what's already available in search results. Pages that merely restate common knowledge receive lower rankings. Compares content depth, technical precision, and unique data points against the existing corpus for a query. Pages with high information gain are rewarded; those with zero gain are treated as redundant.

name: Content Integrity & Decay
definition: Detects content that has become outdated, contradictory, or inconsistent over time. Compares content freshness indicators (last modified dates, copyright years, blog recency) against claims made on the page. Outdated content that contradicts current reality signals neglect and reduces confidence.

name: First-Party Evidence
definition: Evaluates whether content includes proof of real work such as before/after scenarios, specific project outcomes, named team members, and dated work examples. Stock descriptions with no case studies or project details score low.

name: Information Density Ratio
definition: Evaluates how much of the page contains meaningful, useful information versus filler, padding, or generic text. A high ratio means most sentences carry real value. A low ratio indicates bloated content stuffed with marketing language.

name: Personal Experience Narrative
definition: Detects whether the content includes first-hand experience, storytelling, real operational insight, or author bios that demonstrate practitioner-level knowledge rather than secondhand research.

name: Sourcing Integrity
definition: Evaluates whether referenced data sources are clearly cited and verifiable. Checks page content for citations, links to original sources, and properly attributed claims rather than unsupported assertions.

name: Primary Citation Quality
definition: Measures whether the content cites original research, primary documents, or direct evidence rather than rehashing secondary sources. Original data, case studies, and proprietary research score high.

name: Comparative Utility
definition: Measures whether the page helps users compare options, products, services, or approaches with specific pros and cons, rather than simply promoting one option.

name: Niche Expertise Vocabulary
definition: Detects the natural presence of specialized terminology specific to an industry. Genuine expertise uses jargon naturally in context, while surface-level content avoids it or uses it incorrectly.

name: Cost Transparency
definition: Evaluates whether pricing, cost frameworks, or cost breakdowns are explained on the page. Real pricing information visible on the page is a strong information gain signal.

name: Case Study Granularity
definition: Measures whether detailed examples of real work or outcomes are presented with measurable results, specific project details, and concrete evidence rather than vague claims.

name: Opinionated Stance
definition: Detects whether the content expresses a defensible viewpoint rather than neutral marketing copy. Authors who take positions and explain their reasoning demonstrate genuine expertise.

name: Content Decay
definition: Detects outdated references, stale copyright years, old dates, or missing update indicators on the page. How outdated the content appears directly impacts trust and ranking eligibility.

name: Excessive CTA Saturation
definition: Measures the density of calls to action relative to informational content. Too many CTAs overwhelming the content signals a page designed for conversion rather than value.

name: Thin City Pages
definition: Identifies location pages with minimal unique information where only the city name is swapped. Template content patterns are detectable from page content structure and repeated blocks.

name: Auto-Generated FAQ
definition: Detects FAQ sections clearly produced by automated templates with generic, unhelpful questions that add no real value and are designed to inflate page content.

name: Obfuscated Pricing
definition: Detects intentional hiding of pricing to force user contact. Deliberately withholding pricing information that users expect creates friction and signals a less transparent operation.

name: First-Party Data Use
definition: Detects whether the site publishes proprietary data, original research, or unique datasets that cannot be found elsewhere. First-party data is a strong information gain signal.

name: Topical Coverage
definition: Evaluates the breadth and depth of content covering the entity's claimed areas of expertise. Comprehensive topic coverage signals genuine authority to classifiers.

name: Ungrounded Claims
definition: Specific business claims that CANNOT be verified or lack supporting evidence from external sources. Self-claims without corroboration represent trust vulnerabilities.

name: Contradiction Detection
definition: Identifies conflicts between sources - such as website claims contradicting review content, GBP data conflicting with directory listings, or licensing records not matching claimed credentials.

name: Cross-Source Alignment
definition: Measures consistency between website, reviews, directories, GBP data, and external references. High alignment across all sources strengthens entity trust. Low alignment raises suspicion.

name: Pricing Opacity
definition: Identifies patterns of refusal to disclose fees, vague estimates, or bait-and-switch pricing signals found in review complaints and website analysis.

name: Commercial Bias Drift
definition: Identifies 100% transactional CTA content with no educational or informational content. Gets categorized as 'sales collateral' rather than a helpful resource by the information vs. transactional intent classifier.

name: Service Menu Depth
definition: Measures how thoroughly the GBP service menu covers the entity's actual service offerings. Shallow or missing service menus reduce relevance signals.

name: Information Gain Deficiency
definition: Identifies content classified as 'commodity knowledge' or 'sales collateral' by the helpful content system. Generic how-to content without first-party proof, zero original data, and sales-only copy.

name: Lexical Diversity
definition: Measures the variety of vocabulary used in a page. Low lexical diversity suggests templated or repetitive content (repeating the same adjectives like 'quality', 'professional', 'trusted'), while high diversity indicates natural writing with precise, varied vocabulary specific to the industry and region.

name: Syntactic Burstiness
definition: Measures variation in sentence structure and length. Natural human writing contains irregular patterns with a mix of short punchy sentences and longer detailed ones, while AI or templated content tends to produce uniform sentence lengths and robotic rhythm.

name: Semantic Drift
definition: Evaluates natural topic flow across content. Low semantic drift means content stays rigidly on one sales message with robotic topic adherence. High semantic drift shows natural tangents that add depth, like mentioning local conditions, related problems, or seasonal factors.

name: Cliche Density
definition: Tracks common marketing cliches such as 'go the extra mile', 'second to none', 'customer satisfaction is our priority', or 'best of both worlds'. High density reduces informational uniqueness and signals generic content.

name: Idiomatic Regionalism
definition: Detects region-specific language, cultural references, or local dialect markers. Strong presence reinforces local authenticity. Generic American English that could describe any city scores low, while local place names, regional terms, and area-specific knowledge scores high.

name: Proper Noun Density
definition: Measures the presence of specific entities such as equipment brands, team member names, neighborhood names, local landmarks, and certifying bodies. High density increases grounding signals and specificity. Low density means no names, no brands, no locations beyond the city.

name: Technical Precision
definition: Assesses the accuracy and specificity of technical terminology. Low precision shows vague statements like 'we use the latest technology and advanced techniques'. High precision shows details like '48-inch CIPP liner cures at 180F using UV-activated resin, eliminating styrene emissions of traditional steam-cure methods'.

name: Emotional Variance
definition: Measures tonal variability across the text. Flat promotional tone throughout indicates corporate or automated writing. Natural shifts between educational, cautionary, proud, and conversational tones signal authentic human authorship.

name: Nuance Preservation
definition: Tracks whether content acknowledges uncertainty, variation, or context instead of absolute claims. Low nuance shows statements like 'we're the best' and '100% guaranteed'. High nuance shows contextualized claims like 'most homes in this zip code have galvanized supply lines from the 1970s build cycle'.

name: Pattern Repetition
definition: Identifies repeated structural templates across multiple sections or pages. Repeated heading patterns, paragraph structures, and content block layouts often indicate programmatic page generation or template scaling.

name: Pronominal Frequency
definition: Tracks the usage frequency of pronouns such as we, our, you, they, or them. Overuse of 'we' and 'you' in page text suggests corporate boilerplate, while balanced usage suggests a more conversational, natural tone.

name: Passive Voice Saturation
definition: Measures how often passive constructions appear relative to active voice. Moderate usage is normal, but high passive voice saturation often appears in generic or templated content and can signal automated writing.

name: Rhetorical Question Ratio
definition: Measures the presence of rhetorical questions used for engagement. Excessive use can signal sales copy or AI-generated patterns. Overuse of questions like 'Looking for the best service?' is a common pattern in low-quality content.

name: Verb Tense Consistency
definition: Evaluates whether verb tenses shift logically across the text. Natural writing contains expected shifts between past, present, and future tense. Highly rigid tense patterns often indicate templated or AI-generated writing.

name: Adverbial Fluff
definition: Detects unnecessary filler adverbs like 'basically', 'actually', 'essentially', 'extremely', or 'very'. High levels suggest padding or AI-generated content that inflates word count without adding information.

name: Prompt Leakage
definition: Detects artifacts of AI prompting such as instruction fragments, meta-commentary, or phrases like 'As an AI...' left in the text. These indicate content was generated by an LLM and not properly edited.

name: Perplexity Volatility
definition: Measures unpredictability in language patterns across the page. Natural human writing shows moderate volatility, while templated or AI-generated text is highly predictable with uniform information density throughout.

name: Human Presence Signals
definition: Detects visible staff members, technicians, or leadership on the website. Team photos uniqueness, named personnel, and visible human operators establish authenticity and counter the 'faceless corporation' pattern.

name: Team Photo Uniqueness
definition: Detects whether team images are authentic original photos rather than stock photos. Computer vision analysis can identify stock imagery patterns, generic studio setups, and commercially licensed images.

name: Visual Age
definition: Evaluates whether the site design appears outdated through deprecated design patterns, old frameworks, or visual conventions that signal the site hasn't been maintained.

name: Visual Hierarchy
definition: Evaluates whether the page layout guides users through content in a logical, prioritized order. Poor visual hierarchy causes users to miss important information and increases bounce rates.

name: Visual Authenticity Gap
definition: Identifies reliance on stock photos instead of authentic project documentation. Triggers the 'generic business' flag and fails the E-E-A-T experience check from computer vision analysis.

name: Photo Diversity
definition: Evaluates the variety and quality of photos in the GBP listing including team photos, project work, equipment, and facilities. Diverse photo galleries signal authenticity.

name: Watermark Detection
definition: Scans for visible or semi-transparent watermarks from stock agencies like Getty, Shutterstock, Adobe Stock, iStock, or Alamy. Presence of stock watermarks is a clear indicator of non-original imagery.

name: Frequency Domain Noise
definition: Assesses whether the image shows digital signature patterns typical of AI generators including uniform noise patterns, SynthID markers, or unusual pixel-level artifacts.

name: High-Key Uniformity
definition: Measures the light-to-shadow ratio. Studio stock photos show uniform, controlled lighting with soft shadows. Natural photos have uneven, directional light with hard shadows and highlights.

name: Bokeh Depth Estimation
definition: Assesses depth-of-field characteristics. AI and stock images often feature artificially perfect shallow DOF with mathematically smooth bokeh. Real photos have optical imperfections and irregular bokeh shapes.

name: Micro Expression Mismatch
definition: Checks for forced or unnatural facial expressions. Stock models show exaggerated, uniform expressions. AI-generated faces may have subtle asymmetries, teeth artifacts, or expression inconsistencies.

name: Gaze Vector Analysis
definition: Checks if subjects look directly at camera with a 'commercial' gaze pattern. Stock photos favor direct eye contact, while real workplace photos show people engaged in actual tasks.

name: Sanitation Score
definition: Measures how 'clinically clean' the environment appears. Real workspaces have clutter, wear, and personal items. Stock and AI images are sanitized with perfectly arranged props.

name: Product Placement Detection
definition: Identifies generic, unbranded 'hero' objects or props that exist only for visual composition rather than functional use, indicating staged commercial photography.

name: Generic Intent Vector
definition: Overall assessment of whether the image was staged for commercial or stock purposes versus captured in an organic, real-world context, considering props, clothing, environment, and composition.

name: User Interaction Signals
definition: Tracks how users interact with search results. High bounce rates, pogo-sticking back to search, and low dwell time signal that a page didn't satisfy the query. Operates at the query level - if users consistently click a result and quickly return to search, the page is demoted for that specific query regardless of its other signals.

name: Trust & Popularity Integrity
definition: Validates that popularity signals are authentic and naturally correlated. High review counts without corresponding branded search volume or news mentions raise suspicion. Google's systems look for a natural nexus of signals. When one metric is disproportionately high compared to others, its weight is dampened as a precaution, creating a trust ceiling.

name: Review Sentiment & Trust
definition: Extracts patterns from review content to validate entity claims. Google's sentiment extraction identifies keywords and patterns in reviews that either confirm or contradict an entity's claimed expertise. Strong review-to-claim alignment is a powerful trust signal.

name: Branded Search Connection
definition: Measures whether the entity generates branded search volume. Entities that produce branded search queries demonstrate real-world recognition beyond just web presence.

name: Review Sentiment Asymmetry
definition: Detects when reviews mention only generic attributes rather than specific technical services, creating algorithmic doubt about the entity's specialized service delivery capabilities.

name: Citation Utility
definition: Evaluates whether the link serves as a meaningful citation or reference that adds value for readers, versus being placed purely for SEO purposes.

name: Review Volume
definition: Measures the total number of reviews across the GBP profile. Higher volumes provide more data for sentiment analysis and signal business maturity to ranking systems.

name: Review Velocity
definition: Tracks the rate at which new reviews are being acquired. Accelerating velocity signals growing business activity, while decelerating velocity signals decline.

name: Sentiment Consistency
definition: Evaluates whether review sentiment is consistent across different time periods and platforms, or shows concerning patterns like sudden shifts or bimodal distributions.

name: Reviewer Trust
definition: Assesses the trustworthiness of individual reviewers based on their review history, profile completeness, and patterns. Reviews from established, active Google users carry more weight.

name: Response Latency
definition: Measures how quickly the business responds to reviews. Fast, consistent responses signal active engagement and customer care to both users and ranking systems.

name: Response Quality
definition: Evaluates the substance and personalization of owner responses to reviews. Generic template responses score lower than personalized, detailed replies that address specific feedback.

name: NAP Consistency
definition: Evaluates Name, Address, Phone consistency across all directory listings, citations, and web mentions. Inconsistent NAP data fragments entity signals and confuses ranking systems.

name: Press Mentions
definition: Tracks mentions in local news, industry publications, and media coverage. Press mentions are strong prominence signals that validate entity authority.

name: Gemini/AI Inclusion
definition: Evaluates whether the entity appears in AI-generated recommendations and summaries. Entities that surface in Gemini and AI Overview results have stronger entity graph presence.

name: Citation Velocity Asymmetry
definition: Detects high review velocity paired with low branded search demand or lack of corroborating local media and citation growth. This asymmetry signals inauthentic prominence to trust systems.

name: Link Value & Authority Transfer
definition: Evaluates the quality, relevance, and authenticity of inbound links. Assesses source trust, topical alignment, audience overlap, and editorial intent of each link. High-value links from industry peers reinforce entity positioning; toxic or irrelevant links can trigger penalties.

name: Link Toxicity & Safety
definition: Identifies manipulative link patterns including PBNs, paid links, excessive exact-match anchors, and doorway pages. SpamBrain-class systems detect patterns of artificial link building. PBN footprints, unnatural anchor text distributions, and links from known spam neighborhoods trigger link value neutralization or penalties.

name: Entity Link Authenticity
definition: Evaluates whether the business appears in credible external directories and associations such as BBB, Yelp, Clutch, or Alignable, validated via external search signals.

name: Domain Age & Maturity
definition: Evaluates how old the linking domain is. Longer-established domains carry more trust equity. New domains linking heavily can signal artificial link building.

name: Historical Indexing Stability
definition: Checks whether the linking domain has been consistently indexed by search engines or shows drops and recoveries that suggest quality issues or penalties.

name: Anchor Text Relevance
definition: Evaluates the anchor text used for the link. Natural, descriptive anchors transfer topical signals. Over-optimized exact-match anchors can trigger spam detection.

name: Surrounding Text Sentiment
definition: Analyzes whether the text surrounding the link is positive, neutral, or negative. Links in negative contexts can transfer negative sentiment to the target.

name: PBN Pattern Signals
definition: Detects whether the linking source looks like a private blog network site through patterns like thin content, unrelated topics, excessive outbound links, and hosting fingerprints.

name: Automated Content Likelihood
definition: Evaluates whether the linking source appears to use mass-generated or AI-produced content, which reduces the editorial value and trust transfer of the link.

name: Link Scheme Pattern
definition: Identifies whether the link is part of an obvious link exchange, reciprocal linking scheme, or paid link arrangement that violates search engine guidelines.

name: Doorway Page Identification
definition: Checks whether the page containing the link is a doorway or gateway page designed primarily for search engines rather than users.

name: Aggressive Exact Match Anchor
definition: Detects whether the anchor text is over-optimized with exact match keywords, which is a strong signal of manipulative link building to spam detection systems.

name: SGE Extraction Potential
definition: Evaluates whether AI systems can use this link to connect the two entities in AI-generated search summaries and recommendations.

name: Trust by Association
definition: Evaluates whether the source's reputation enhances the target's trustworthiness. Links from highly trusted domains transfer trust signals that benefit the target entity.

name: Composite Link Value
definition: The aggregated score combining source trust, topical alignment, toxicity risk, and agentic utility into a single 0.0-1.0 link value (LV) with veto override capability.

name: Schema & Structured Data
definition: Evaluates the depth and accuracy of structured data markup. JSON-LD schema for Organization, LocalBusiness, Product, and FAQ types enables search engines to extract and validate entity information. Missing or inaccurate schema creates ambiguity in entity classification.

name: Schema Grounding Depth
definition: Measures how extensively structured data (JSON-LD) describes the entity and services on the page. Deep, complete schema enables richer understanding by search engines and AI systems.

name: SGE/AI Overview Compatibility
definition: Evaluates whether the page structure supports extraction by AI-generated summaries and search generative experiences. Well-sectioned content with clear answers is more likely to appear in AI overviews.

name: Content Sectioning Clarity
definition: Evaluates heading hierarchy (H1, H2, H3, H4) and logical page structure from the scraped page. Clear, semantic heading organization enables both users and crawlers to parse content efficiently.

name: Breadcrumb Logic
definition: Checks whether page navigation clearly describes site structure through logical breadcrumb paths that help both users and search engines understand page context.

name: Canonical Signal Health
definition: Verifies that canonical tags correctly identify the authoritative URL from the scraped page meta data, preventing duplicate content issues and consolidating ranking signals.

name: API Integration Readiness
definition: Measures whether structured content could be easily consumed by APIs and third-party systems. Well-structured data with clean markup enables broader content distribution.

name: Structured FAQ Schema
definition: Detects implementation of FAQ structured data with genuine, useful Q&A content from the scraped page. Properly marked up FAQs can earn rich results in search.

name: Semantic HTML
definition: Evaluates whether the page uses proper semantic HTML elements (article, section, aside, nav, main) rather than generic divs, improving machine readability and accessibility.

name: Crawlability
definition: Evaluates how easily search engine crawlers can access and index site content. Blocked resources, JavaScript rendering requirements, or robots.txt restrictions can prevent content discovery.

name: Indexation Depth
definition: Measures how many of a site's pages are actually indexed by search engines relative to total pages published. Low indexation ratios signal quality concerns or crawl barriers.

name: Internal Linking Coherence
definition: Evaluates whether the site's internal link structure creates logical topical clusters and helps search engines understand content relationships and hierarchy.

name: Tech Stack Currency
definition: Measures whether the underlying technology is modern and maintained. Deprecated JavaScript libraries, old CMS versions, and outdated frameworks signal technical neglect.

name: Technical Depth Deficit
definition: Detects generic service descriptions lacking technical specificity, causing content to be relegated to the 'surface-level content' tier by information gain and helpful content classifiers.

name: Schema Sync
definition: Measures alignment between website structured data (JSON-LD) and GBP listing data. Mismatches between schema and GBP create entity confusion.

name: Scaled Content System
definition: Detects content created at scale that provides little unique value between pages. Templated service pages, thin city pages, and repetitive structures trigger domain-level dampening. When a significant portion of pages share 80%+ identical boilerplate text, value propositions, and structure, the system classifies them as unhelpful, creating a domain-level quality anchor that suppresses the entire site.

name: Content Scraping Traces
definition: Detects duplicate content that appears verbatim on other sites across the internet, checked via search queries for exact phrases from the page.

name: Fake Expert Personas
definition: Detects fabricated author profiles, non-existent experts, or synthetic bios used on the page to simulate authority. Often detectable by reverse image search or lack of external presence.

name: Review Velocity Anomaly
definition: Detects unusual bursts or patterns in review acquisition that suggest manipulation. Sudden spikes of reviews followed by silence, or clusters of generic language, indicate inauthentic signals.

name: Lead Generation Front
definition: Identifies sites designed primarily for capturing leads rather than providing actual services. Pages with minimal value content that exist purely to funnel contact information.

name: Service Page Uniqueness
definition: Measures how unique each service page is compared to others on the same site. Low uniqueness ratios where service pages share most of their content trigger scaled content detection.

name: Template Overreliance
definition: Detects when a site relies heavily on a single template across multiple service or location pages, creating patterns that trigger scaled content detection at the domain level.

name: Review Manipulation
definition: Detects patterns suggesting fake or manipulated reviews including burst reviews with generic language, bimodal rating distributions, or synthetic pattern indicators like identical phrasing across multiple reviews.

name: Spam Detection Risk
definition: Calculates a 0.00-1.00 risk score for potential spam signals in the GBP listing including fake reviews, keyword-stuffed names, and manipulative tactics.

name: Scaled Content Risk
definition: Evaluates the ratio of templated, low-value pages to unique content pages. High ratios of zero-traffic URLs, city page templates, and exact-match internal anchors trigger domain-level quality dampening.

name: Intent Capture Speed
definition: Quantifies how quickly a motivated visitor can find what they need and take action. Slow intent capture increases bounce rates and signals poor user satisfaction to Google's interaction classifiers.

name: Action Visibility
definition: Evaluates how prominently calls to action are displayed. Hidden phone numbers, buried contact forms, and missing above-the-fold CTAs create conversion leakage.

name: Trust Before Ask
definition: Measures whether trust signals (reviews, credentials, guarantees) are presented before conversion points. Asking for user action without establishing trust first reduces conversion rates.

name: Choice Simplicity
definition: Evaluates whether the user path to conversion is simple and clear. Too many options, confusing navigation, or unclear next steps create decision paralysis and increase bounce rates.

name: Form Field Entropy
definition: Measures the complexity and number of form fields relative to the conversion goal. Excessive form requirements create friction that reduces completion rates.

name: Mobile Navigation Depth
definition: Measures how many taps or interactions are required to reach key content on mobile devices. Deep navigation structures on mobile create friction and signal poor user experience.

name: Sticky Element Overlap
definition: Detects whether sticky headers, footers, or CTAs overlap with page content, blocking readability or interaction on various screen sizes.

name: Conversion Leakage
definition: Identifies points in the user journey where potential conversions are lost due to UX issues such as hidden phone numbers, non-sticky CTAs, excessive form requirements, or delayed trust signals.

name: Emergency Intent Friction
definition: Detects UX barriers for urgent service requests. High bounce rates on pages that should serve emergency intent signal failure to satisfy 'urgent intent' to NavBoost-class interaction systems.

name: Search CTR
definition: Measures click-through rate from search results to the GBP listing. Higher CTR signals relevance and attractiveness to users for the queries being served.

name: Direction Requests
definition: Tracks the volume of direction/navigation requests through the GBP listing. High direction request volume signals genuine local demand and physical visit intent.

name: Booking Conversion
definition: Measures conversion rates through GBP booking or appointment features. Active booking usage signals a business that invests in the Google ecosystem.

name: Query Deserves Freshness
definition: Evaluates content recency and update velocity. Static sites miss opportunities to align with seasonal search trends and lose temporal relevance signals. Sites that remain static during peak demand periods lose current relevance signals. Content calendars, timely blog posts, and updated imagery maintain temporal authority.

name: Update Velocity
definition: Measures how frequently the site publishes new content or updates existing pages. Active publishing signals ongoing investment and relevance. Static sites gradually lose temporal authority.

name: Content Rotation
definition: Detects whether testimonials, blog posts, gallery images, or news updates appear regularly. Active content rotation signals an engaged, operating business.

name: Blog Post Recency
definition: Tracks how recently informational or blog content has been published. Stale blogs with the last post months or years ago signal abandonment to both users and search systems.

name: Stale Internal Links
definition: Detects links pointing to outdated, removed, or inactive pages within the site. Broken internal links signal maintenance neglect and degrade crawl efficiency.

name: Review Momentum
definition: Measures the ongoing flow and velocity of reviews over time. Distinguishes 'Fading Giants' (old reviews, decelerating momentum) from 'Rising Stars' (recent activity, accelerating reviews).

name: Quality Trajectory
definition: Tracks whether review ratings are improving or declining by comparing recent reviews (last 20) against the lifetime average. Detects 'Service Decay' when recent sentiment is worse than historical.

name: Service Decay Signal
definition: Detects declining customer satisfaction patterns in recent reviews compared to historical patterns. A pattern of recent negative reviews after historically positive ones indicates operational problems.

name: Business Stability
definition: Evaluates the longevity, ownership continuity, and operational consistency of the company. Years in business, domain age, name/address change history, and ownership signals all factor in.

name: Ownership Changes
definition: Detects recent name changes, address changes, or management turnover that may indicate business instability or attempts to distance from negative history.

name: Seasonal Stagnation
definition: Detects year-round generic promotion versus alignment with seasonal demand cycles. Missing the 'current relevance' boost during peak demand periods costs visibility when it matters most.

name: Post Recency
definition: Tracks how recently the entity has published Google Business Profile posts. Regular posting signals an active, engaged business to local ranking systems.

name: Hours Integrity
definition: Verifies that business hours listed in GBP are accurate and up to date, including special hours for holidays. Incorrect hours lead to customer frustration and trust signals.

name: Q&A Freshness
definition: Evaluates the quality and recency of questions and answers on the GBP listing. Owner-verified answers to genuine questions strengthen the listing's information value.
